skill.name: prpm-json-best-practices
skill.description: Guides creation and maintenance of prpm.json manifests for PRPM packages, collections, file metadata, tags, eager loading, scripts, and publishing checks.
skill.summary: Create consistent PRPM package manifests for single packages, multi-package repositories, collections, and publishing workflows.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The reviewed findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, example JSON, schema URLs, and local validation snippets. I found no evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, unauthorized network calls, or malicious filesystem access in the reviewed files. The skill documents PRPM manifest practices and does not include executable package code.

content.value_statement: PRPM publishers need manifests that are complete, consistent, and ready for review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through package fields, collections, tags, files, and publish checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains required prpm.json fields for single-package and multi-package manifests.
Shows how to define collections that reference local and published packages.
Guides tags, naming, versioning, and file path organization.
Documents eager and lazy activation settings for skills and agents.
Provides validation and publishing workflow checks before release.
Describes conversion hints for Cursor, Claude, Kiro, Copilot, Continue, Windsurf, and Agents.md.
limitations: Does not publish packages or run PRPM commands by itself.
Does not validate a manifest against the schema automatically.
Does not replace security review of lifecycle scripts or packaged files.
Examples use placeholder names, paths, and repository URLs.

use_cases.title: Create a first package manifest
use_cases.description: Create a new prpm.json with required metadata, files, tags, and supported format fields.

use_cases.title: Organize a prompt package repository
use_cases.description: Organize multiple skills, agents, rules, and commands in one repository without duplicate names.

use_cases.title: Design installable collections
use_cases.description: Bundle related packages into installable collections with versions, required flags, and clear inclusion reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PRPM manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a prpm.json for one Claude Code skill. Ask for missing package details, then draft the required fields.

prompt_templates.title: Review my manifest for completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my prpm.json for required fields, tag quality, file paths, and version consistency. Explain each required fix.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-package repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a prpm.json for a repository with several skills, agents, and rules. Group entries by privacy, format, and subtype.

prompt_templates.title: Add collections and conversion hints
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my manifest with collections and conversion hints. Keep local packages separate from installed dependencies in prpm.lock.

output_examples.input: A publisher wants to package one Claude skill with a README and examples.
output_examples.output: A completed manifest plan with required metadata, file list, tags, and a validation checklist.

output_examples.input: A team has five related prompt packages in one repository.
output: Recommended package ordering by privacy, format, and subtype.
Naming guidance to prevent duplicate registry entries.
Publishing checks for versions, files, and tags.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants a collection for a TypeScript workflow.
output_examples.output: A collection outline with package purposes, version ranges, required flags, and concise inclusion reasons.

best_practices: Use full project-root file paths for every packaged file.
Keep tags specific, lowercase, and written in kebab-case.
Validate required fields, versions, duplicate names, and file existence before publishing.
anti_patterns: Adding installed packages from prpm.lock to prpm.json.
Mixing string file entries and object file entries in the same files array.
Using prepublish scripts when prepublishOnly is the intended publish-time hook.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps authors create and review prpm.json manifests for packages, collections, and publishing workflows.

faq.question: Does it install PRPM packages?
faq.answer: No. It documents manifest structure for publishers. It does not install packages.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude Code skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Claude Code skill entries, file paths, eager settings, and related metadata.

faq.question: Does it support multi-package repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains package arrays, duplicate prevention, ordering, and shared repository metadata.

faq.question: Can it validate my manifest automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide validation steps, but an external validator or PRPM command must perform validation.

faq.question: Should prpm.lock entries be copied into prpm.json?
faq.answer: No. prpm.lock tracks installed dependencies. prpm.json defines packages that you publish.
